p.challenge: Build 4 sentences from 'A Letter to God' — pick the right determiner: many/few for countable, much/little for uncountable

items.text: There were very few clouds in the sky in May.
items.hint: Clouds can be counted. 'Very ___' means not many.

items.text: The hail ruined many fields in the village.
items.hint: Fields can be counted. It means a large number.

items.text: There was little water left in the well.
items.hint: Water cannot be counted. It means not much.

items.text: The hailstorm did much damage to the crop.
items.hint: Damage cannot be counted. It means a lot of.

p.title: A Letter to God
p.challenge: Put Lencho's story in order — then spot the irony in the last card

panels.t: Lencho's ripe corn field needs only rain.
Rain comes, then big hailstones fall.
The hail ruins the crop. Not a leaf remains.
Full of faith, Lencho asks God for 100 pesos.
The postmaster collects money from his staff.
He can send only a little over half: 70 pesos.
Lencho: 'Post office employees are crooks!'

p.title: Dust of Snow (Robert Frost)
p.challenge: Rebuild the poem line by line. Rhymes help: crow/snow (a), me/tree (b)

panels.t: The way a crow
Shook down on me
The dust of snow
From a hemlock tree
Has given my heart
A change of mood
And saved some part
Of a day I had rued.

p.challenge: Make the 3 sentences the lesson needs: simple past (he became President), present perfect (South Africa has changed), past perfect (he had spent 27 years in prison)

sentences.meaning: 10 May 1994: a finished action at a stated time.
Since 1994: a past action linked to now.
Before his release in 1990: the earlier of two past actions.

future.continuous: He [will be spending] 27 years in prison.
future.perfect: He [will have spent] 27 years in prison.

p.title: A Tiger in the Zoo (Leslie Norris)
p.challenge: Order the 5 stanzas: cage → where he SHOULD be (wild) → back to the cage. Feel the contrast!

panels.t: Cage: he stalks the few steps of his cage.
Wild: he should lurk in grass by the water hole.
Wild: snarling at houses at the jungle's edge.
Cage: locked in a concrete cell, ignoring visitors.
Cage: at night he stares at the brilliant stars.

p.challenge: Report 4 statements: move the tense back (can → could, will → would, am → was) and change pronouns and time words

items.from: 'I can't do it,' Tara whispered.
items.text: Tara whispered that she couldn't do it.

items.from: Mr Rao said, 'I will be right here.'
items.text: Mr Rao said that he would be right there.

items.from: The young seagull said, 'I am afraid to fly.'
items.text: The young seagull said that he was afraid to fly.

items.from: Tara said, 'I am diving today.'
items.text: Tara said that she was diving that day.
items.hint: am diving → was diving; today → that day

p.challenge: Read each clue's hint and pick the right modal of deduction: must (almost sure), can't (sure it is NOT true), might (only possible)

items.text: The lights are on, so they must be home.
It can't be Ravi because he is in Delhi today.
It might snow in Manali this week.
Someone must have entered the locked music room.
items.hint: Fresh petals on the piano: almost certain. Past = modal + have + V3.

p.title: The Ball Poem (John Berryman)
p.challenge: Order the poem's moments: from losing a ball to learning what loss means

panels.t: The boy's ball goes bouncing down the street.
Merrily over: there it is in the water!
The boy stands rigid, trembling, staring.
The poet does not buy him another ball.
The boy learns what losing something means.
He must learn to bear loss: he is growing up.

p.title: From the Diary of Anne Frank
p.challenge: Put Anne's diary story in order, from her birthday gift to Mr Keesing's change of heart

panels.t: Anne gets a diary on her 13th birthday, 1942.
She names it Kitty: the friend she can confide in.
Talking in class: extra essay 'A Chatterbox'.
Still talking: 'An Incorrigible Chatterbox'.
'Quack, Quack, Quack…': Anne writes a funny poem.
Mr Keesing takes the joke and stops the essays.

p.challenge: Report 4 questions: yes/no → asked if/whether; wh- → keep the wh-word. Use statement order, no question mark

items.from: Mr Keesing asked Anne, 'Why are you talking again?'
items.text: Mr Keesing asked Anne why she was talking again.

items.from: He asked, 'Are you ready?'
items.text: He asked if I was ready.

items.from: She asked, 'Where do you live?'
items.text: She asked me where I lived.
items.hint: Keep 'where'; do you live → I lived

items.from: Riya asked her friend, 'Do you like the book?'
items.text: Riya asked her friend whether she liked the book.

p.challenge: Build the lines from 'Amanda!' and the lesson, then pick each sentence type and its end mark

items.text: Don't bite your nails, Amanda!
Did you finish your homework, Amanda?
How tall the mountains are!
Amanda dreams of being a mermaid.
Sit up straight.

p.challenge: Turn each past habit into 'used to' or 'would' (remember: 'Did you use to…?', 'didn't use to')

items.from: The baker came every morning. (He doesn't now.)
items.text: The baker used to come every morning.

items.from: The children rushed to the gate every day.
items.text: The children would rush to the gate every day.

items.from: Did you play gilli-danda as a child?
items.text: Did you use to play gilli-danda as a child?

items.from: A big banyan tree stood here once.
items.text: There used to be a big banyan tree here.

items.from: She didn't like spicy food then.
items.text: She didn't use to like spicy food.

p.challenge: Glimpses of India: build the comparative or superlative each clue needs

words.meaning: Coorg's hills are ___ than the plains (comparing two).
the most big of all (double the g!)
Long adjective: the best-looking of three or more.
best known of all (long adjective → most)

p.challenge: Order the adjectives: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose

items.text: She bought a lovely little old red Kashmiri shawl.
A tiny old wooden stall sold hot banana fritters.
Mist curled over the rolling green tea hills.

p.challenge: Build 5 sentences and choose the verb that agrees with the subject

items.text: Each of the otters has a name.
One of my pets is a parrot.
items.hint: 'One of the…' takes a singular verb.

items.text: Laddoo and Mishri are best friends.
Either Ravi or his sisters are coming.
The teacher, along with her students, is visiting the zoo.
items.hint: 'Along with' → agree with the first subject.

p.challenge: Turn adjectives into adverbs (-ly) that tell HOW Mij the otter did things

words.meaning: Mij swam ___ in the bath (in a smooth, lovely way).
The otter bobbed up, chirping ___ (y → i).
Mij splashed ___ (with a lot of sound; y → i).

p.challenge: Drop 'like' / 'as' and turn each simile into a metaphor, just as Sandburg makes the fog a cat

items.from: The fog comes like a cat, on little feet.
items.text: The fog comes on little cat feet.

items.from: The classroom was as noisy as a zoo.
items.text: The classroom was a zoo.

items.from: Her smile is like sunshine.
items.text: Her smile is sunshine.

items.from: Dadi's heart is as precious as gold.
items.text: Dadi's heart is pure gold.

p.challenge: Report 4 commands and requests: requested / warned / ordered / advised + person + (not) to + verb

items.from: 'Uncle, please open the window wider,' Chintu said to the conductor.
items.text: Chintu requested the conductor to open the window wider.

items.from: 'Don't lean out,' the conductor said to Chintu.
items.text: The conductor warned Chintu not to lean out.

items.from: 'Stand up at once!' the teacher said to the class.
items.text: The teacher ordered the class to stand up at once.

items.from: 'You should drink more water,' the doctor said to Papa.
items.text: The doctor advised Papa to drink more water.

p.title: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
p.challenge: Put the ballad in order and find the funny twist: who is the real hero?

panels.t: Belinda lives with Ink, Blink, Mustard and Custard.
Custard wants a safe cage; all call him a coward.
One night a pirate climbs in at the window.
Mustard flees; Ink and Blink hide.
Custard jumps at the pirate and gobbles him up.
The others boast they would have been braver.
And Custard still cries for a nice safe cage.

p.challenge: Join the ideas of Kisa Gotami's story with the right connector: reason, contrast or result

items.text: Kisa Gotami wept because her only son had died.
She went from house to house, but every family had lost someone.
Death comes to every family, so grief is shared by all.
She found no mustard seed. However, she found the truth.

p.challenge: Make 6 opposites with the right prefix: un-, in-, im- (before p/m), il- (before l), ir- (before r), dis-

words.meaning: not honest: the opposite of inner beauty

p.title: The Proposal (Anton Chekhov)
p.challenge: Put the scenes of the one-act play in order: how do two quarrels get in the way of one proposal?

panels.t: Lomov arrives at Chubukov's in evening dress.
He asks for Natalya's hand; Chubukov is happy.
Lomov and Natalya quarrel over the Oxen Meadows.
Chubukov joins the quarrel and Lomov leaves.
Natalya learns why he came: "Bring him back!"
New quarrel: whose dog is better, Guess or Squeezer?
They get engaged, and start quarrelling again!

p.challenge: Make 5 adjectives from nouns to describe the comic characters of 'The Proposal'

words.meaning: likes to argue, like Lomov and Natalya
anxious and jumpy, like Lomov when he arrives

p.challenge: Turn 4 active sentences into the passive: be + past participle, and keep the tense the same

items.from: Mrs Pumphrey fed Tricki.
items.text: Tricki was fed by Mrs Pumphrey.

items.from: The vet examines the dog.
items.text: The dog is examined by the vet.

items.from: They have cured the dog.
items.text: The dog has been cured.
items.hint: Present perfect: has been + V3; the doer can be left out

items.from: The boy will walk the dog.
items.text: The dog will be walked by the boy.

p.title: A Triumph of Surgery
p.challenge: Put Tricki's story in order, then see why the title is ironic

panels.t: Mrs Pumphrey overfeeds Tricki with cream cakes.
Tricki grows fat and lazy, and falls ill.
The vet, James Herriot, takes him to his surgery.
For two days Tricki gets no food at all.
He runs and plays with the other dogs.
Gifts of eggs, wine and brandy: the vets enjoy them!
Tricki goes home fit: 'A triumph of surgery!'

p.challenge: Make the 3 narrative tenses of 'The Thief's Story': background (Anil was sleeping), earlier event (Hari had decided), main event (Hari turned back)

sentences.meaning: The earlier of two past events.

future.continuous: Hari [will be deciding] to run away.
future.perfect: Hari [will have decided] to run away.

sentences.meaning: A main event in the story.

p.title: How Hari changes
p.challenge: Order Hari's journey from thief to a young man who values trust: the evidence for a character sketch

panels.t: Hari, a thief, meets Anil at a wrestling match.
Anil gives him work, and Hari cooks for him.
Anil teaches Hari to write his name.
One night Hari steals Anil's money.
At the station he lets the train leave without him.
He sees that learning is worth more than money.
He returns the money. The notes are still wet.

p.challenge: Build 4 conditionals and choose 'will' (real possibility) or 'would' (imaginary)

items.text: If the police come, they will search the room.
items.hint: First conditional: If + present, will + verb

items.text: If I were a spy, I would carry a camera.
items.hint: Second conditional: If + past (were), would + verb

items.text: If we hurry, we will reach on time.
If I were you, I would apologise.

p.title: The Midnight Visitor
p.challenge: Use the sequence words to put Ausable's clever escape in order

panels.t: First, Ausable and Fowler enter Ausable's room.
Then they find Max waiting with a pistol.
Next, Ausable complains about the 'balcony'.
Suddenly a knock! "It must be the police."
Max climbs out of the window onto the balcony.
Finally, Max screams: there is no balcony!
It was only a waiter bringing drinks.

p.title: A Question of Trust
p.challenge: Put Horace Danby's story in order: how does the careful thief end up cheated?

panels.t: Lock-maker Horace robs a safe a year for rare books.
He plans carefully and enters an empty house.
A young woman says she is the lady of the house.
He takes off his gloves and opens the safe for her.
She leaves with the jewels.
His fingerprints are on the safe: he is arrested.
Nobody believes him. The cheat was cheated!

p.challenge: Build crime words: is each one a PERSON or a CRIME? Use the clues

words.meaning: PERSON who breaks into a building to steal
CRIME of breaking into a building to steal
PERSON who moves goods secretly and illegally
CRIME of moving goods secretly and illegally

p.title: Footprints without Feet (H.G. Wells)
p.challenge: Order Griffin's adventures: why is being invisible far from easy?

panels.t: Two boys in London see footprints but no feet.
Griffin, a scientist, made himself invisible.
To stay unseen he goes unclothed, and is cold.
He sleeps in a London store; seen, he escapes.
A theatre shop gives him bandages and dark glasses.
At an inn in Iping, Mrs Hall finds him strange.
He throws off his clothes and escapes, unseen.

p.title: Letter to the editor
p.challenge: Arrange the 8 parts of a letter to the editor about misuse of science, from top to bottom

nodes.info: The Editor, name and address of the newspaper.
e.g. Subject: Unsafe flying of drones over crowded festival grounds
Introduce the issue, give reasons and examples, suggest solutions, close politely.

p.title: The Making of a Scientist
p.challenge: Put Richard Ebright's journey in order, from butterflies to DNA

panels.t: As a child, Richard Ebright collects butterflies.
Mother gives him 'The Travels of Monarch X'.
He tags monarch butterflies for research.
His first science-fair project does not win.
He tests if viceroy butterflies copy monarchs.
In college: a theory of how cells read DNA.

p.title: Science club members

ask.question: Membership rose every year except one, when it fell slightly. Tap that year.

p.challenge: Read the trend for your analytical paragraph: membership rose every year except one, when it fell slightly. Tap that year.
Join each pair with who, which, whose or that, as Maupassant's story needs

items.from: Rani loved to look rich. Rani borrowed a silk sari.
items.text: Rani, who loved to look rich, borrowed a silk sari.

items.from: The sari tore on a nail. She wore the sari proudly.
items.text: The sari, which she wore proudly, tore on a nail.

items.from: The cousin laughed. Rani had borrowed the cousin's sari.
items.text: The cousin whose sari Rani had borrowed laughed.

items.from: Matilda lost the necklace. The necklace was fake.
items.text: The necklace that Matilda lost was fake.

p.challenge: Make the abstract nouns behind 'The Necklace': what cost the Loisels, and what could have saved them?

words.meaning: too much pride in looks and status: Matilda's flaw
being modest about oneself: the opposite of pride
being happy with what you have: the opposite of greed
telling the truth: it could have saved the Loisels
not showing off: the opposite of vanity

p.title: Bholi (K.A. Abbas)
p.challenge: Order Sulekha's story: how does school change the girl everyone called 'Bholi'?

panels.t: Sulekha, called Bholi, fell off a cot as a baby.
Smallpox marks; she stammers and is mocked.
A girls' school opens; Bholi is sent there.
A kind teacher helps her speak and read.
Old Bishamber agrees to wed her, then wants dowry.
Bholi firmly refuses the greedy man.
She will teach at the school that changed her.

p.challenge: Build 5 sentences and pick the modal for each job: ability, permission, obligation, advice or no necessity

items.text: At first Bholi could not speak clearly.
May I come in, ma'am?
You must wear a helmet on a scooter.
You look tired, so you should rest.
You needn't bring lunch to the camp.
items.hint: No necessity: lunch will be served

p.challenge: Join Greek and Latin roots to build 6 science words the Martians would need

words.meaning: instrument for viewing far-off things (tele = far)
instrument for viewing very small things (micro = small)
a device to hear a voice from far away
a device that picks up small sounds and makes them louder
a 'star sailor': a person who travels in space
the study of the earth's rocks
the written story of a person's life

p.challenge: Build 5 sentences and choose the right homophone each time (their/there, read/reed, knight/night…)

items.text: The Martians left their spaceship near the library.
Think-Tank could not read the book correctly.
The knight rode bravely through the dark.
Please write your name on the form.
The Martians wanted to know the Earth's secrets.
